note: The living knowledge feed. Add an entry here and it appears on the site — this is how LMC COMMAND grows with input.

entries.title: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (128GB) chosen as the render node
entries.body: 128GB unified memory holds large video + language models at once. 'Killed the $200/month AI bill' — the everyday model cost moves on-device.

entries.title: LTX 2.3 is the anchor local video model
entries.body: Apache 2.0, runs on NVIDIA / Apple Silicon / AMD Radeon at 24fps. Open license means no per-render metering on the Ryzen node.

entries.title: SkyReels for cloud-burst hero shots
entries.body: Omni-reference, unlimited length. Kept for frontier-quality bursts, not the everyday default.

entries.title: Blender + TRIPOINT for the 3D stage
entries.body: Free triangulation tool feeding layout, camera and blocking before AI video coverage.

entries.title: Markerless motion capture from plain video
entries.body: Performance capture without a suit or stage — mocap that used to cost hundreds of thousands, now accessible.

entries.title: Claude Code + MCP is the autonomy layer
entries.body: Agentic monitoring and orchestration — this is LMC COMMAND itself: agents that run and watch the studio.

entries.title: Local LLM for the writing & agent layer
entries.body: A free, powerful open model in the 128GB pool handles briefs, prompts and agents with zero cloud tokens.

entries.title: Client call: the command center is the in-house heartbeat
entries.body: Confirmed with Jen (ops + developer on the build): LMC COMMAND is the in-house system to run all projects and tasks for Leo and the team — always-changing, many parallel projects (construction, cabinetry, lighting, studio buildout, TV show, client work).

entries.title: The 1 a.m. brain — capture, don't lose
entries.body: Leo generates ideas and follow-ups at all hours, including overseas vendor calls at 10pm–1am. Priority feature: dead-simple thought capture from the phone, triaged into projects later. Nothing gets lost.

entries.title: Own-your-Cheqroom: track down to the cardellini
entries.body: ~90% of gear is in Cheqroom, but per-SKU/QR pricing means small grip (C-stands, arms, knuckles, cardellinis ~$100 ea) is untracked and walks away. Plan: in-house QR labels + piece-level check-in/out, own the system, drop the subscription.

entries.title: Anti-subscription: consolidate the AI stack
entries.body: LMC pays professionally for 'every kind of AI' and more. Kemp (editor) to pull the full list; we build the subscription ledger and cut list. Validates the own-the-engine thesis.

entries.title: Mac side needs M4 — current M1/8GB won't carry it
entries.body: Their Mac is M1 / 8GB / 2020 — not enough. Minimum M4 for the Mac environment; heavy AI/render stays on the owned Ryzen AI Max 395 128GB node.

entries.title: Handoff + extraction prompts delivered to Jen
entries.body: Jen builds as a developer on her side and will pull the LMC ecosystem from her ChatGPT thread. Delivered: DEVELOPER_HANDOFF.md and EXTRACTION_PROMPTS.md (CSV/MD handoff format she can ingest directly).

entries.title: Task & Project Command + Idea Inbox are live on the board
entries.body: command.html reads the exact extraction-prompt CSVs (lmc_projects_tasks.csv, lmc_ideas_followups.csv) as seed data. Where-are-we-on-everything by project, My tasks, one-field capture with triage, CSV import/export.

entries.title: Team sign-in: GitHub-backed, Work Official is owner/admin
entries.body: Members sign in with their own GitHub token; the owner grants/revokes access from the repo's collaborators. Every change is a commit under the person's name in data/board.json — remote access from any device, additive and reversible.

entries.title: Gemini guides Jen through setup
entries.body: The board's Guide tab runs Gemini with the onboarding doc, handoff, extraction prompts and live board state. docs/JEN_ONBOARDING.md is the written version; docs/GEMINI_GUIDE_GEM.md makes it a standalone Gem.
